riskAnalysis: Mandatory third-submission root-cause analysis: R01 correctly required an exhaustive addendum-authority denial matrix with byte-exact no-mutation proof. The R02 implementation created internally bound real-Git variants and added dual-file snapshots to the newly written grouped cases, but it treated the older exact-chain test and wrong-candidate tail assertion as already sufficient. That assumption caused uneven assertion granularity: some denials proved both planning/backlog.yaml and the GCR state unchanged, while retained altered/missing/partial and wrong-candidate cases did not. Independently, a workspace test hard-coded the then-next remediation evidence filename; once each adverse attempt legitimately tracked that file, the fixture stopped modeling 'the next absent canonical transition artifact' and failed at later repository states. The systemic root cause was coupling proof helpers and fixture identities to individual test blocks/current attempt count instead of encoding the invariant once and reusing it. Corrective action: one b01_control_snapshot helper now captures both canonical control files and is applied before and after every addendum denial; the workspace test discovers the first absent canonical remediation evidence path rather than naming an attempt. Preventive action: all future denial additions must use the shared snapshot helper, and lifecycle fixtures must derive sequential artifact identity from repository state. The complete 27-test suite passes at the exact candidate, directly exercising these corrections. This test-only strict descendant preserves R01/R02 ledgers and grants no ordinary amendment, task, Wave, hold-release, or gate authority.
